message.reasoning:
I need to make a decision for my turn in Monopoly.

I have $698 cash and am on Reading Railroad. I hold a dark blue monopoly with Boardwalk at one house and Park Place at zero. I recently mortgaged Vermont Avenue.

I will build one house on Park Place for $200. This brings both dark blue properties to one house each under even-building rules. I will leave about $498 in cash and avoid mortgaging Kentucky Avenue.

Boardwalk at two houses would rent $600 and Park Place at two would rent $500. I am checking opponent holdings to gauge how much pressure this creates.

Opponent p1 has liquid assets of roughly $1,164. Opponent p3 has about $1,127 in liquid assets. Opponent p4 has $951 cash plus property. No opponent holds a complete color-group monopoly.

Opponent p4 has roughly $1,406 in liquid assets. Boardwalk at two houses would rent $600 and not bankrupt anyone. Three houses would rent $1,400 and could force p1 and p3 into bankruptcy. I am weighing whether to mortgage Kentucky Avenue for an extra $110 to buy four houses instead of stopping at two.

Five houses would cost $1,000. I can only afford three. I will stop at two houses on each dark blue property and leave about $98 in cash.

Opponent p3 is on Water Works and will roll next. It takes nine spaces to reach Park Place.

The probability of landing on Boardwalk is only about 17 percent. With zero houses, the dark blue rent is just $35 per property. I must build one house on Park Place now to raise the rent to $175.

I will not trade Kentucky Avenue. It blocks opponent p3's red monopoly and I am avoiding trades under $400. Acquiring Indiana from p1 is unlikely this turn. I must build on Park Place now before p3 rolls.
